patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient has experienced gradual yellow discoloration of the skin and generalized pruritus over the past 2 weeks. He also reports a decreased appetite and a weight loss of 6.3 kg (14 lb). The patient’s stool has been pale, and his urine is very dark. Three years ago, he had an episode of acute upper abdominal pain, which was managed with IV fluids, NSAIDs, and dietary modification. The patient has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 years. He has a 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.
patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Episode of acute upper abdominal pain treated three years ago. History of long-term alcohol consumption and smoking.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Stopped alcohol consumption three years ago; 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.

objective_for_doctor: Assess the patient and determine the cause of jaundice, pruritus, weight loss, pale stool, and dark urine.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: Over the past two weeks, my skin has turned yellow and I’ve had generalized itching. My appetite has decreased and I’ve lost about 6.3 kg, with pale stools and very dark urine.
Doctor: Have you noticed any abdominal pain or discomfort, especially in the right upper quadrant or upper middle area?

Patient: I don’t have significant abdominal pain right now, but I did have an episode of upper abdominal pain about three years ago that improved with IV fluids and NSAIDs. Since then, I’ve been mostly okay until these recent symptoms started two weeks ago.
Doctor: Have you taken any new prescription medications, over‑the‑counter drugs, herbal supplements, or changed your alcohol consumption in the past month?

Patient: I haven’t started any new prescription medicines, and I don’t use over‑the‑counter drugs or herbal supplements regularly. I also haven’t changed my alcohol intake—I've been abstinent for about three years now.
Doctor: Have you had any fever, chills, or night sweats since these symptoms began?
Patient: I haven’t had any fever or chills, and I haven’t noticed night sweats either.
Doctor: Have you ever been diagnosed with gallstones, gallbladder disease, or any prior biliary or pancreatic surgery?

Patient: I was never told I had gallstones or gallbladder disease, and I haven’t had any biliary or pancreatic surgery. I did have that earlier upper abdominal pain episode, but it was managed without any procedures.
Doctor: Have you had any recent travel, new tattoos or piercings, unprotected sexual encounters, or intravenous drug use that could increase your risk for viral hepatitis?
Patient: No recent travel, no new tattoos or piercings, and I haven’t had any unprotected sexual encounters or IV drug use.
Doctor: Do you have any history of chronic medical conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, autoimmune disease, or prior liver disease?

Patient: I haven’t been told I have diabetes, hypertension, high cholesterol, autoimmune disease, or any prior liver disease. My main past issue was that earlier episode of upper abdominal pain about three years ago, but I haven’t had chronic conditions diagnosed since then.
Doctor: Have you noticed any swelling in your abdomen (ascites), swelling in your legs, or any easy bruising or bleeding?
Patient: I haven’t noticed swelling in my abdomen or legs, and I don’t think I’ve had any unusual bruising or bleeding.
Doctor: Do you have any personal or family history of inflammatory bowel disease (such as ulcerative colitis or Crohn’s disease) or any known liver or pancreatic cancers in close relatives?
Patient: No, I don’t have any family history of inflammatory bowel disease, and I’m not aware of any liver or pancreatic cancers in close relatives.
Doctor: Do you currently smoke cigarettes or have you smoked in the past?
Patient: Yes, I currently smoke cigarettes and I’ve smoked for about 50 years, roughly a pack a day. I haven’t been able to quit.
Doctor: Have you ever had an episode of pancreatitis or been told you have high triglycerides or gallstones in the past?

Patient: I haven’t been told I had pancreatitis before, and I don’t know of any high triglycerides or gallstones being found. My only prior episode was that upper abdominal pain about three years ago, and it settled with IV fluids and NSAIDs.
Doctor: On exam, do you have a palpable, non‑tender gallbladder (Courvoisier’s sign) or any other abdominal masses you can feel?
Patient: I don’t think I have any noticeable abdominal swelling, and if you examine me there isn’t any mass I can feel or any tenderness when my belly is pressed.

Doctor: Have you had any blood work done recently—especially liver function tests or a complete metabolic panel—and if so, can you tell me what the results were (bilirubin, AST/ALT, alkaline phosphatase, GGT)?
Patient: I haven’t had any blood work done yet, so I don’t know my bilirubin, AST/ALT, alkaline phosphatase, or GGT levels. If you order labs today, I can get those results back to you.
Doctor: On physical exam, do you have any visible signs such as yellowing of the eyes (scleral icterus), spider‑like blood vessels on the skin, or redness of the palms (palmar erythema)?
Patient: Yes, I do have noticeable yellowing—both in my skin and my eyes—but I haven’t noticed spider-like blood vessels or red palms.
Doctor: Have you ever received blood transfusions, organ transplants, or undergone long‑term hemodialysis that might increase your risk for viral hepatitis?
Patient: No, I’ve never had a blood transfusion, organ transplant, or long-term hemodialysis. I don’t have any known risk factors like viral hepatitis from those situations.
